scenes.title: 맞았다는 사실이 먼저 보이게
lines: If an attack lands and the opponent's pose barely changes, it's hard to tell whether you hit. A sharp bend that lingers for an instant can sell the impact before you check the numbers. In Tekken, Lili’s feet lift under the blow. Even without the health bar, the bend in her back and knees tells us who was hit. We'll build a hit reaction by looking at its first pose, its transition and where the next blow must land. A hit reaction means the character has been struck. Its first job is showing that change of state. A tiny change from the idle pose can disappear on a small screen. Lean back or redirect the limbs so the outline alone shows a different state. That outline is the silhouette. Hit stop briefly arrests the motion on impact, letting the pose register. That makes the first reaction pose much more than a passing in-between drawing. We'll compare a subtle reaction with a distinct silhouette on the same character at the same size. Can you still feel the hit without seeing color or the face?

scenes.title: 큰 자세 변화도 연결은 필요하다
lines: A big change can look disconnected if the body jumps instantly into another shape. A short transition connects the pose before contact to the first reaction. Calculating intermediate states between two poses is called interpolation. Define the hand in front of the body and beside the head, then generate positions between them. Our demonstration shows where the character passes between those starting and ending poses. Aim for a short, clear transition into an easily readable reaction. Its length depends on the game.

scenes.title: 몸의 모양과 캐릭터 위치를 구분하기
lines: That transition reveals another problem. Imagine a blow reaching the fingertips of an outstretched arm. Fold the arm back and the torso can appear quite far from the attacker. Holding the contact pose clarifies where the hit landed. Showing the reaction quickly emphasizes the change of state. Decide which information should register first. Separate the visible shape of the body from the character's overall position. A hitbox can deliver an attack, and a hurtbox can receive one. These regions serve a different purpose from the visible model. The root node determines the position of the character as a whole. In a combo, the second blow needs to connect after the first. Moving the root along with the recoiling torso can carry the target out of reach. Watch the floor reference while we compare the two cases on the grid. Knowing whether the body or the whole character moved tells us what to fix.

scenes.title: 맞은 곳과 충격의 크기
lines: The characters now stay in position for the next hit. Next we need to show where the hit landed and how hard it was. Identical reactions at the head and legs hide information about the point of impact. A light tap and a blow that sends someone reeling need different reactions. Suppose we have high, middle and low hits, each in three strengths. That's three high reactions, three middle reactions and three low reactions. Three times three gives nine combinations. Change only height, then hold height and change strength. These nine cells are an example. Choose reactions for the information your game needs to communicate. Knockback may also need airborne poses and a specific kind of rotation.

scenes.title: 같은 반응을 다른 몸에 옮기면
lines: Even after choosing reactions, each new character adds work. With the same arm angle, one hand may reach the cheek while a longer arm extends above the head. When Donkey Kong spreads his arms outside his torso, they cover a different area than human arms raised at the same angle. Identical bone rotations don't guarantee the same silhouette. Humanoids can share more motion than round characters, quadrupeds or characters carrying large weapons. An arm can cover the torso and a weapon can hide the face. Copying an existing file is only the start of building reactions for a new character. Keep the meaning of the hit, but find a reaction that suits that body.

scenes.title: 날아갈 때도 팔다리가 읽혀야 한다
lines: However the body is built, the test is the same. Does the pose read on a small screen? When limbs overlap in side view, even a big movement can hide what bends. Twist the torso and separate the arms to reveal the hands and legs. There is a purpose to breaking symmetry. It lets us distinguish the parts responding to the blow. With the camera fixed, compare the same airborne pose as the torso turns. Check both the still image and normal-speed playback.

scenes.title: 짧은 순간에 남기는 강한 반응
lines: For a fleeting instant you can push the difference further. A pose that looks distorted on pause can communicate a powerful hit in motion. Judge the information that moment leaves during play. The reaction must show that the hit landed, convey its force and preserve the position for the next action. Shape the silhouette, refine the transition and vary the reaction with hit height, strength and body type. Together these choices let attacker and defender read the same impact.
